entities.name: PMID:16335173
observations: In vitro/in vivo study reported median log10 CFU/mL of 0 for gypsum casts treated at 2450 MHz/900 W for 5 min, versus 4 when impressions were treated with 0.07% NaOCl for 3 min before pouring; untreated controls had 6. Chemical arm was not cast-treatment like-for-like.

entities.name: PMID:25083033
observations: In Type III dental-stone casts, 900 W microwave treatment for 5 min and 0.5% NaOCl each produced about 5-log10 CFU/mL reduction against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa and were reported equivalent.

entities.name: PMID:38317034
observations: In 90 Type IV die-stone casts, microwave was more effective microbiologically than chemical immersion or spray (P<0.010 and P<0.001); microwave increased surface roughness, while none of the methods significantly changed dimensions.

entities.name: PMID:39657937
observations: Type IV stone biofilm study compared microwave irradiation for 1–5 min with chlorhexidine, NaOCl, and neem; microwave and NaOCl showed comparable potency against C. albicans, and results varied by organism.

entities.name: PMID:24082984
observations: Dental-stone carrier study reported high-level disinfection with 600 W microwave for 3 min and with 0.06% NaOCl for 2 min; this was a parameter comparison, not a broad cast-property study.

entities.name: Microwave cast disinfection
observations: Multiple studies directly compare microwave with chemical disinfection for microbial control of dental gypsum/stone casts; outcomes range from equivalent efficacy to greater efficacy with microwave.

Direct comparative physical-property evidence is limited: one 2024 study reported increased surface roughness after microwave treatment but no significant dimensional change with any method; comparative hardness/strength and surface-detail evidence is insufficient.
